# darwinkit import

The Objective-C framework bindings in `core:sys/darwin/*` and `vendor:darwin/*` are generated by
[darwodin](https://github.com/harold-b/darwodin) (Harold Brenes), which binds the macOS and iOS SDK
headers with `csgen` and merges both SDKs into a single `darwinkit` tree using
`#+build darwin:default` and `#+build darwin:ios`.

Regenerating darwinkit needs a Mac with Xcode. This directory only holds the step that brings an
existing darwinkit tree into this repository:

```
python vendor/darwin/_gen/import_darwinkit.py <path/to/darwodin/darwinkit>
```

Last imported from darwodin `08a4e2827` (macOS 26.2 and iOS 26.2 SDKs).

## Placement

| Collection        | Frameworks |
|-------------------|------------|
| `core:sys/darwin` | CoreFoundation, CoreGraphics, CoreText, DiskArbitration, FSEvents, Foundation, IOKit, Security |
| `vendor:darwin`   | everything else |

Packages in `core:sys/darwin` never import `vendor:darwin`; the script fails if a regeneration would
make one do so. darwinkit's `ObjectiveC` package is not imported, `core:sys/darwin/ObjectiveC` is
maintained by hand. `vendor:darwin/CoreVideo` is hand-written as well.

## What the script changes

- Relative imports (`"../Foundation"`) become collection imports.
- darwodin's own `libc` and `mach` packages are replaced by `core:sys/posix` and `core:sys/darwin`
  (`MACH_MAP` and `LIBC_MAP` in the script). A new symbol without a mapping stops the import.
- Overload groups whose members are all class methods get `objc_is_class_method=true`, so that
  `NS.String.stringWithContentsOfURL(...)` resolves.
- Every method whose last parameter is a `^^NS.Error` out-parameter gets an Odin-style wrapper:

  ```odin
  library, err := device->newLibraryWithSource(source, options)
  ```

  The wrapper returns `(res: T, err: ^NS.Error)`, `(ok: bool, err: ^NS.Error)` for `bool` methods,
  or just `err`. Methods returning `instancetype` return a pointer to their own class. The raw method
  is always available with an `_error` suffix (`Device_newLibraryWithSource_options_error`), and
  overload groups refer to the wrapper. When a wrapper would collide with another method of the same
  name or signature (usually a deprecated variant without `error:`), only the raw method is
  provided.
- Enums which are flag sets in the SDK but which csgen emitted as plain enums (`FLAG_ENUMS`) become a
  `bit_set` of the same name over an element enum of bit indices, e.g. `MTL.TextureUsage` is
  `bit_set[MTL.TextureUsageFlag]`. A member equal to 0 or to a combination of bits becomes a
  constant, e.g. `MTL.TextureUsage_Unknown :: MTL.TextureUsage{}`; a combination which sets bits
  no member names becomes a `transmute`, e.g. `MTL.Stages_All`.
- Flag enums which also hold multi-bit fields (`FLAG_ENUM_FIELDS`), such as `UI.ViewAnimationOptions`
  with its animation curve in bits 16-17, are converted the same way, except that the field values
  become constants rather than flags:

  ```odin
  opts := UI.ViewAnimationOptions{.Repeat, .Autoreverse} | UI.ViewAnimationOptions_CurveEaseIn
  ```

  Every bit of a field or of a mask gets an element `_Bit<n>`, so that the constants are ordinary
  sets (`UI.ViewAnimationOptions_CurveLinear` is `{._Bit16, ._Bit17}`) and `opts & ~Mask` clears the
  same bits as `opts &~ Mask`. A field is read back through its mask, where the SDK has one, and
  replaced by clearing the mask first:
  `writing & NS.DataWritingOptions_FileProtectionMask == NS.DataWritingOptions_FileProtectionComplete`,
  `writing = writing &~ NS.DataWritingOptions_FileProtectionMask | NS.DataWritingOptions_FileProtectionNone`.
  `NS.SaveOptions` (exclusive values) and `CF.SocketCallBackType` (a callback gets one type) stay enums.
- Enum members mangled by csgen's prefix removal are renamed (`ENUM_MEMBER_FIXES`), e.g.
  `AVFoundation.CaptureSystemPressureFactors` has `SystemTemperature` rather than `ystemTemperature`.
- Enum members which keep a C-style `k` prefix lose it, as csgen does for the rest: `kSecPaddingNone`
  becomes `Sec.SecPadding.None` and `kCGLPFADoubleBuffer` becomes `.DoubleBuffer`. Stripping stops
  at the end of the enum's own name (`kEAGLRenderingAPIOpenGLES1` becomes `.OpenGLES1`), and a name
  which would start with a digit gets a leading `_` (`kColorSync8BitInteger` becomes `._8BitInteger`).
- Plain enums which csgen emits as bit_sets (`NOT_FLAG_ENUMS`) become enums again, e.g.
  `Security.SSLSessionOption`, whose members are option indices 0 to 9.
- Known problems in the generated output are patched (`KNOWN_FIXES`, `ALIAS_FIXES`).
- AppKit's `Foundation.Exports.odin`, which csgen generates so that `import NS "vendor:darwin/AppKit"`
  provides all of Foundation, also gets aliases for Foundation's hand-written top-level declarations
  (`NS.AT`, `NS.scoped_autoreleasepool`, …).
- csgen's one file per class or protocol is merged into one file per family or topic, see below.

## File grouping

csgen writes every class and protocol to its own file. `group_files` merges them, much as Apple's
headers do, using only the names and the superclasses:

1. **Families.** A type goes with the type its name extends, ignoring `Mutable` and role suffixes
   (`GROUP_ROLE_SUFFIXES`: Descriptor, Delegate, State, …): `MTLRenderPipelineState`,
   `MTLRenderPipelineDescriptor` and `MTLRenderPipelineReflection` go together, and `NSMutableArray` goes with `NSArray`.
2. **Subclasses named after their superclass**, and descriptor variants: `MTLRenderCommandEncoder` goes
   with `MTLCommandEncoder`, `NSInputStream` with `NSStream`, `MTLTileRenderPipelineDescriptor` with
   `MTLRenderPipeline`. Not for the general bases in `GROUP_GENERIC_BASES`, so `NSScrollView` is not
   put with `NSView`.
3. **Small types** go with their superclass when it is in the same package: `NSDimension` with `NSUnit`.
4. **Topics.** Families and single types sharing their first word go in one file, named after the
   words they all share: `MTLRender.odin`, `NSTable.odin`, `MKLookAround.odin`.
5. **Kinds.** Single types still on their own that share a last word are put together: `NSViews.odin`.
6. **Overrides** (`GROUP_OVERRIDES`) for what the name rules get wrong, e.g. `NSCoding` goes in `NSObject.odin`.

Types are only merged with types that have the same build tag. In a package that mixes build tags,
the macOS-only or iOS-only part of a group goes in `<name>_macos.odin` or `<name>_ios.odin`, as
csgen already does for the package files (`GameKit_macos.odin`). The package files themselves,
`Foundation.Exports.odin` and the hand-written files are left as they are.

## Hand-written files

Every generated file starts with:

```
// Generated by vendor/darwin/_gen/import_darwinkit.py from darwinkit. DO NOT EDIT.
```

The script only overwrites or deletes files that start with that line, and refuses to overwrite a
hand-written file of the same name. Odin-specific helpers belong in separate files next to the
generated ones (e.g. `Foundation_extras.odin`) so that they survive a re-import.

A hand-written procedure named `<generated procedure>_slice` is added to the overload group of that
generated procedure by the script, turning a single generated method into a group whose original
method is renamed with a trailing `_`. This is how `Metal_extras.odin` lets
`encoder->setViewports(viewports[:])` sit alongside `encoder->setViewports(&viewport, 1)`. Since the
script looks for these procedures in the destination package, run it again after adding one.
